title: 649. Minimum Factorization

examples.explanation: 48 splits as 6 x 8; arranging the digits increasingly gives 68, the smallest layout.
13 is prime above 9, so no digit layout exists.

hints: Pull factors greedily from 9 down to 2 so the digit multiset stays small and sortable.
If a remainder above 1 survives, the task is impossible (answer 0); otherwise sort digits increasingly and reject overflows past 2^31-1.
